## Passages and paraphrase locations

<a id="bohm-on-dialogue-undated-handout-q001"></a>
### q001 · PDF 2–3

Dialogue permits meaning to develop through participants. Discussion's contest for a winning opinion is contrasted with inquiry into assumptions inherited through culture and identified with oneself. A felt threat to an opinion can disclose those assumptions.

**Locator:** PDF 2–3.

**Status:** Paraphrase only; no quotation admission.

**Verification:** The bounded reading and consulted-carrier scope are recorded in this source house. This heading repair adds no new source-verification claim.

<a id="bohm-on-dialogue-undated-handout-q002"></a>
### q002 · PDF 4–6

Tacit habits and group roles enter the inquiry. Facilitation serves a practice capable of continuing without a permanent directive authority. Suspension neither enacts nor suppresses an assumption: its activity can become available for attention. Bohm's unnamed anthropological anecdote does not establish a universal Indigenous practice.

**Locator:** PDF 4–6.

**Status:** Paraphrase only; no quotation admission.

**Verification:** The bounded reading and consulted-carrier scope are recorded in this source house. This heading repair adds no new source-verification claim.

<a id="bohm-on-dialogue-undated-handout-q003"></a>
### q003 · PDF 7–9

Participation in developing meaning need not make opinions identical or erase individuals. Frustration, anger and anxiety belong to the inquiry; shared meaning is not guaranteed harmony. These are descriptions and proposals for practice, not controlled evidence of an intervention's outcomes.

**Locator:** PDF 7–9.

**Status:** Paraphrase only; no quotation admission.

**Verification:** The bounded reading and consulted-carrier scope are recorded in this source house. This heading repair adds no new source-verification claim.
